checks: Source fbf10959836f7b72 §2, (3)–(4), supplies the same lower bound and completion. The frozen proof replaces residual augmentation for the lower bound by a direct product-density construction.

For every right section the normalizer is at least c>0 and is measurable by Fubini. The right density is m/b, the left density is at most m/c, and both are at most one. The measure is supported on the closed relation and has total mass m.

Finite measures of bounded mass on the compact product have weakly compact closure. Support in G and both marginal domination conditions are weakly closed, the latter by testing nonnegative continuous functions. The continuous mass functional therefore attains a maximum.

After subtracting used marginals, the residual product divided by a−g has exactly the right residual marginal and uses at most the left residual. The case g=b is taken separately so no zero denominator occurs. The completion may leave G.

overlap.comparison: Pairs finitely many integer bases with externally provided edge capacities and prescribed product couplings of their fibers. It does not yield an attained continuous matching constrained to a general closed relation.
Optimizes a finite loss-capacity matching on a specific disjoint-interval graph. Its capacity model does not impose or use Lebesgue section lower bounds on an arbitrary compact product.

readability: The quantified statement and proof agree.

summary: The direct section-normalized density gives the lower bound, with attained maximum and valid residual marginal completion.
